name: StoreInstanceHandle
status_promotion: RUNTIME_TESTED for the single documented startup call and scenario below; not VERIFIED, and not a claim about other levels, modes or the surrounding startup sequence. The Lead applies the manifest patch.
scope: One startup invocation of retail 0x0048F0D0 StoreInstanceHandle against the candidate symbol _StoreInstanceHandle in a single paired scenario: retail level 1, windowed mode (arguments 'window level1'), working directory /Users/haseeb-mir/Downloads/IGI, the same reviewed typed probe hooked at the native entry and the typed state VA before the primary thread resumed, retail observed first and the candidate only after retail was confirmed gone.
reason: The candidate entry point calls _StoreCommandLine with WinMain's lpCmdLine and then _StoreInstanceHandle with WinMain's hInstance, in retail order and before window creation. The sequential paired capture observed exactly one call on each side under the same conditions, and all 31 compared typed fields are identical: the argument is non-null, is the process module base (the process instance handle class), is consistent with the first observation, and equals the HINSTANCE of the game window the process created; the return aliases the argument and the stored word; the previous stored word was null on both sides; and the stored word aliases the argument and the return. The captured candidate image (f9f3b9ee..., receipt 158f189c...) validated against the current tree and engine/src/retail/core/app_startup_natives.cpp at capture start and after capture. This is runtime parity for the single documented startup call, not a VERIFIED claim.

window_instance_contract.definition: The "instance handle the window was created with" is read from GWL_HINSTANCE (-6) of the game window created by the instrumented process, identified by the per-side window class: retail "Innerloop", candidate "IGI.Retail.ModelScene". The probe hooks CreateWindowExW and CreateWindowExA and reads the created HWND on return, with a visible-window poll over the same class as a fallback.
window_instance_contract.not_compared_across_processes: The window class name and the raw HINSTANCE address differ between processes and are not compared. The compared facts are: a window of the declared class exists, its HINSTANCE is non-null, and it equals the argument, the stored word and the module base in that process.

diagnostic_evidence.note: A post-launch diagnostic enumeration (not part of the acceptance probe) found the candidate game window class IGI.Retail.ModelScene, visible, plus hidden Wine IME windows; this identified the per-side class before the final capture.

limitations: Single call and single scenario: exactly one invocation was observed per side at level 1, windowed, command line "window level1", one game-data working directory. The argument consistency field is therefore true over one call; the retail call site 0x0048F5FA is statically unique, but this capture does not exercise a second call or another path.

The accepted candidate image is f9f3b9ee... (receipt 158f189c...), built by concurrent work at 10:11:34 UTC. The task-context image 11f93920... is no longer present; attempt 1 tested it and observed the same 24 primary typed fields matching but lacked the candidate window relation. The current source digest 337c5d57... is unchanged and the native body is identical. A later concurrent rebuild would supersede this image/receipt pair.

The candidate window class is "IGI.Retail.ModelScene" (diagnostic model-scene shell), while retail uses "Innerloop". The class names are per-side identification and are not compared; only the HINSTANCE relations are part of the native contract. The candidate class is not claimed to be retail-equivalent.

The window relation is read at CreateWindowExA/W return via GWL_HINSTANCE; the final capture used the at-creation hook on both sides. The visible-window poll fallback was not needed. Visibility, window style, title and class equivalence are outside the compared contract.

The driver observation bound was 30 s after the first observed call (settle 45 s), not the precedent 5 s. This is a timing parameter, identical on both sides; the observed window relations arrived within 2.405 s (retail) and 0.206 s (candidate) of the call. Escape was still delivered at >= 2 s by the unchanged action probe.
The retail caller main 0x0048F530 discards EAX after 0x0048F5FA, so the returned alias is observed through the Interceptor return value, not through a retail consumer.

Pointer values are process-local and were never compared as raw addresses. The compared facts are classes and within-process aliasing relations (argument, stored word, return, main module base, created window HINSTANCE).

Attempts 1-4 are retained as failed/partial evidence; only the final capture is the acceptance capture. Attempt 4 was disturbed by concurrent work in this shared worktree, and attempt 2 preflight waited for a foreign probe. The final preflight was clear on the decisive Frida process list; the host advisory after capture lists other agents' analysis commands, not games.
This is runtime evidence for one native call. It says nothing about other natives, rendering, input, terrain, AI or any deferred subsystem, and it does not promote VERIFIED.
establishes: Retail 0x0048F0D0 executes exactly once in the level 1 windowed startup and stores the WinMain hInstance word to 0x005C8BC0, returning the argument in EAX.
The current candidate _StoreInstanceHandle executes exactly once at the same point in its WinMain, stores the hInstance word to its InstanceHandle global and returns the argument.

On both sides the argument is non-null, is the process instance handle (equal to the main module base), is consistent with the first observation, and equals the HINSTANCE of the game window the process created.
On both sides the return aliases the argument and the stored word; the previous stored word was null; the store changed the word and the stored word aliases the argument.

The paired capture ran retail first, then the candidate after retail was gone, with both executables spawned suspended and the same probe installed before resume; both binary digests and the candidate receipt were recorded and validated.
does_not_establish: Runtime parity beyond the single documented call, level and mode; multiple calls, other levels, fullscreen mode, other command lines or other working directories were not captured.
Equivalence of the surrounding startup sequence, window class, window style/title/visibility, rendering, input, terrain or any other native.
A VERIFIED status for 0x0048F0D0 or for the game. The capture is single-call runtime evidence.
That a later candidate rebuild is equivalent; the tested image and receipt digests bind only the captured bytes.
